criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use a horizonless oblique top-down map with diagonal infrastructure axes.
Both frame a river basin between industrial and urban masses.
different: REFERENCE has a lower, more perspectival landscape view; CANDIDATE is steeper and more orthographic.
REFERENCE frames two separated siting landmarks across a broad valley; CANDIDATE tightly frames one dense network.

evidence.observation: Broad oblique valley framing includes distant terrain, separated sites, and strong depth recession.
Steeper oblique framing centers a compact urban-industrial network on visible diamond ground axes.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both distribute factories, roads, utility corridors, and settlement masses around a river.
Both contrast dense industrial nodes with some open or rocky ground.
different: CANDIDATE fills most of the map with continuous buildings and roads; REFERENCE preserves a broad open central valley.
REFERENCE separates the city and industrial plant into distinct masses; CANDIDATE merges several facilities into a denser central corridor.

evidence.observation: Large open valley separates the upper-right city from the lower industrial complex.
Buildings, paved blocks, plants, and utility routes occupy nearly the entire central map.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both show a dark blue, winding channel passing between industrial districts.
Both attach infrastructure crossings or routed corridors near the banks.
different: REFERENCE has a broader, deeper-looking channel with brighter reflections and more pronounced banks.
CANDIDATE water is narrower and darker, while its crossings read more as overlaid routes than a prominent physical bridge.

evidence.observation: Broad reflective S-curving river runs from the upper valley to the lower-left edge.
Narrow dark channel bends through the center and exits toward the lower-left.
A substantial industrial bridge visibly joins both banks near the lower plant.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: In both, generating plants are dominant facilities and pylons remain slender repeated landmarks.
Both use compact utility nodes and larger urban or industrial silhouettes to establish hierarchy.
different: REFERENCE site plants are compact within a wide landscape; CANDIDATE generators are much larger relative to nearby blocks and route spacing.
REFERENCE gives the lower substation a major landmark footprint; comparable CANDIDATE utility nodes are less dominant.

evidence.observation: Remote plant remains compact relative to mountains, towers, and corridor length.
Central generating complex occupies several city blocks and towers over nearby pylons.
Large cyan-framed substation forms a prominent lower-map landmark.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both combine blackened metal, soot-brown soil, dark concrete, and restrained amber illumination.
Both use cyan highlights against warm industrial midtones with cohesive mechanical detailing.
different: REFERENCE is warmer, hazier, and more painterly through the landscape midtones.
CANDIDATE is colder and near-black, with sharper high-frequency ground and building texture.

evidence.observation: Sepia-brown terrain, softened concrete, warm lamps, and smoky atmospheric grading dominate the world.
Soot-black terrain and crisp metallic buildings retain the same warm-amber and cyan accent family.
Blackened riveted metal and inset panels closely echo the reference industrial finish.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both distinguish cyan energized conductors from amber planned or alternate routing.
Both repeat pylons along long corridors and visually connect routes to major facilities.
different: REFERENCE uses thin wire-like spans with consistently visible tower attachment; CANDIDATE uses thick glowing polylines that sometimes overpower or float over pylons.
REFERENCE routes are simpler to trace, while CANDIDATE overlaps cyan loops, amber dashes, and dense structures.

evidence.observation: Thin amber and cyan spans follow repeated towers with clear plant and substation endpoints.
Thick cyan multi-line routing and amber dashed paths traverse a dense field of pylons and buildings.
Cyan outer-grid conductors remain visibly attached across individual tower spans.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use a top status rail, vertical left construction kit, and tall right inspector in dark industrial chrome.
Both organize comparison information with amber and cyan framed cards integrated over the map.
different: CANDIDATE chrome is more segmented and ornate, with generally smaller, denser typography.
REFERENCE gives more area to large site-cost cards and oversized actions; CANDIDATE adds denser route cards and a large empty lower well.

evidence.observation: Simple riveted top rail presents large centered status values.
Segmented metallic top rail preserves the same status-and-resource hierarchy with denser ornament.
Wide right inspector contains two large comparison cards and prominent build-state actions.
